subject: Mental Models
title: Beyond First Order
description: Learn Beyond First Order in one minute.

hook.text: Australia introduced cane toads to eat beetles destroying sugarcane.

buildup.text: First-order effects are immediate and obvious. Second-order effects are the consequences of the consequences.

discovery.text: Most people stop at first order: if we do X, Y happens. Systems thinkers ask: and then what? And after that?

twist.text: Second-order effects are often the opposite of what was intended. Rent controls reduce housing supply.

climax.text: Before any decision, ask 'and then what' at least three times.

punchline.text: First effects are obvious. Real consequences hide in the second and third.

quiz.question: What are second-order effects?
options: The immediate result of an action
The consequences of the consequences of an action
Effects that are twice as strong
